title: apf HTTP-proxy model blocked for Max-plan Claude Code (Anthropic third-party-auth policy)
description: Investigation 2026-05-21: routing claude -p through apf to api.anthropic.com fails 100% with 429 rate_limit_error (generic Error body, no ratelimit headers). Root cause is EXTERNAL: Anthropic policy since ~April 4 2026 blocks Pro/Max subscription OAuth tokens from non-first-party use. A proxy hop makes the request non-first-party; Anthropic detects it below the HTTP layer (forwarding ALL client headers + the query string did NOT help -> transport/TLS fingerprint or token binding). Direct claude -p works; via-apf is fully blocked. Sources: HN 47069299, anthropics/claude-code issue 28091, gsd-2 issue 3772. Implication: apf as an HTTP proxy in front of Claude Code does not work for Max-plan users. apf still works for API-key auth and OpenAI-compatible upstreams (oMLX etc). Decision needed: (a) require an Anthropic API key for the Claude path, (b) pivot to agent-side integration (Claude Code hook / MCP) per ARCHITECTURE.md Open Question 1, (c) document the constraint and scope apf to API-key + OAI-compatible. Do NOT circumvent the detection -- TLS-fingerprint spoofing evades an anti-abuse control and violates Anthropic ToS.
notes:
HOOK RESEARCH 2026-05-21 (claude-code-guide agent, Claude-Code-doc-cited): hooks / Agent SDK CANNOT do the bidirectional round-trip apf needs.
 - UserPromptSubmit: can inject additionalContext, CANNOT rewrite the prompt -> cannot mask outgoing content.
 - PreToolUse: CAN modify tool_input -> token resolution inside tool calls works.
 - PostToolUse: READ-ONLY -> cannot re-mask tool results before the model sees them.
 - No hook (Stop / none) can modify the model response text before display -> cannot unmask the response.
 - Agent SDK exposes the same hooks, no request/response middleware -> no way to wrap the messages() call.
 - An HTTP proxy on ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is the ONLY supported mechanism for bidirectional request/response transformation.

THE BIND: apf needs bidirectional interception. The only mechanism is an HTTP proxy. Anthropic blocks HTTP proxies for subscription (Free/Pro/Max) OAuth. => There is currently NO viable mechanism to run apf as a full privacy filter for Claude Code on a subscription plan -- not as a proxy (blocked), not as a hook (insufficient).

STILL VIABLE: apf as an HTTP proxy for OpenAI-compatible / local agents (Cursor, Aider, Codex, Cline, local models via oMLX) -- fully works. Core IP (detector, vault, tool-call-boundary resolution) intact + reusable. apf for Claude Code via an API key works but the user ruled that out (audience mismatch).

NEEDS A USER DECISION -- strategic re-scoping, not an engineering call: (a) re-scope apf to the OpenAI-compatible + local ecosystem, drop Claude-Code-on-subscription as a target; (b) keep apf as a research artifact / wait for Anthropic to offer a first-party privacy-filter extension point; (c) something else. The PoC did its job: it validated the filter AND surfaced that the proxy delivery collides with Anthropic policy for the primary audience.
close_reason: Resolved: delivery-model decision recorded in docs/sessions/2026-05-22-apf-dtq-strategy.md. Pursue all -- Anthropic feature request, Hermes-first dev/release, keep Claude warm. Workstreams: apf-3kr apf-suc apf-liv apf-hrc.

title: Anthropic request masker does not re-mask tool_use blocks — resolved value leaks back to the model
description:
Found 2026-05-20 by a live claude -p test through apf. Claude itself flagged it: 'my Grep pattern field came out as a fully-formed email address (mara.delacroix@privat-example.de) instead of the literal token I intended to pass.'

Flow: apf resolves tool_use.input on the RESPONSE path (apf -> client) so the local executor gets real values — correct. But on the next turn the client replays the assistant message, now carrying the RESOLVED tool_use, in the request. apf._mask_part handles type=='text' and type=='tool_result' only — it has no 'tool_use' branch — so the replayed tool_use passes through UNMASKED and the resolved original reaches the upstream model.

This violates the core no-leak contract: the boundary-resolved value must never surface back into the LLM context. Multi-turn tool use on the Anthropic path leaks every resolved tool argument back to the model on the following turn.

The OpenAI path does NOT have this bug: openai_shape._mask_message re-masks assistant tool_calls via _mask_tool_call / _walk_json_mask. The Anthropic _mask_part is missing the symmetric tool_use branch — an asymmetry, not a design choice.
design: _mask_part: add a branch for type=='tool_use' that walks the input JSON structure and re-masks string leaves through _mask_text, mirroring openai_shape._walk_json_mask. Note: re-masking is deterministic (vault: same original -> same token), so the replayed tool_use collapses back to the same <REF_N> the model originally emitted. Also check the streaming Anthropic path (sse.py) and whether tool_use can appear in non-assistant roles.
acceptance_criteria: A replayed assistant tool_use with a resolved value is re-masked before forwarding upstream; covered by a test; claude -p multi-turn tool use no longer shows the model its own resolved tool arguments.
close_reason: _mask_part re-masks tool_use.input via _walk_json_mask; verified by live claude -p (model no longer sees its resolved tool args). 4 unit tests.

title: apf over-masks Claude Code's operational context — agent receives unintelligible input
description:
First live test of apf in front of real Claude Code (claude -p with ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=apf, 2026-05-20 — the apf-nia / apf-76s target scenario).

A ONE-sentence user prompt ('use Grep to search for the email mara.delacroix@privat-example.de') produced a 213-entry vault: PERSON=95, URL_LOCAL=36, LOCATION=34, API_KEY=11, NOTE_SENSITIVE=13, DATE=9, PATH=5 ...

Cause: Claude Code injects large operational context into the messages array — CLAUDE.md content, <system-reminder> blocks, environment info, tool schemas, prior turns. apf's detector runs on ALL of it. mask_system=False does not help: this context lives in messages (user-turn / system-reminder content), not the top-level system field.

The detector over-fires catastrophically at this scale: the tool name 'Grep' was masked as PERSON. PERSON precision is ~0.48 on the FP benchmark; across a multi-thousand-token agent context that is dozens of false masks of operational tokens.

Result: Claude DECLINED — 'I can't carry out that request ... contains unresolved placeholders: Grep — the tool name ... the email address ... dozens of <REF_N> placeholders ... probably worth fixing at the source.' The model could not read its own tool names or instructions.

This is the apf-76s effect (model reads opaque tokens as missing info) at full scale, but dominated by detector false positives on operational tokens, not user PII.
design:
apf is currently not usable in front of Claude Code. The masking scope — mask everything PII-shaped in the whole request — is incompatible with a coding agent whose payload is mostly operational context (instructions, tool schemas, file paths, code in tool results), not user PII.

Directions for discussion (NOT decided):
- Scope masking to genuine user-authored message turns; exclude harness-injected context (system-reminders, CLAUDE.md injection, tool schemas, environment blocks).
- Tool results carrying code/file content: masking shreds code — needs an explicit policy.
- Detector precision becomes a correctness blocker, not a tuning nicety: 'Grep'->PERSON must not happen.
- Reframes apf-76s: before 'does Claude tool-call on masked tokens' can be tested, apf must stop shredding the context.
acceptance_criteria: apf in front of claude -p: a simple PII tool-call prompt completes; vault contains only the genuine user PII (single digits, not 200+); Claude does not flag unintelligible placeholders.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE confirmed 2026-05-20 by capturing a real Claude Code request (claude -p -> dump server).

Structure: messages = ONE user message with 7 content parts. Parts 0-5 are each a <system-reminder>...</system-reminder> block (superpowers skill text, agent-type list, MCP instructions, the 18KB skills catalog, hooks, the # claudeMd CLAUDE.md injection) — 38,454 chars of harness scaffolding. Part 6 is the genuine user input ('hello', 5 chars). apf masks all 7 -> 213 vault entries from ~5 chars of real payload.

The top-level system field (3 blocks, the Claude Code system prompt) is already skipped by mask_system=False — correct. The problem is the harness context that lives in messages as <system-reminder>-wrapped user-turn parts.

PROPOSED FIX (structural, deterministic — no heuristics): in the request maskers, skip <system-reminder>...</system-reminder> regions. They are a stable Claude Code convention marking harness-injected context. Genuine user text, tool_result content, assistant content are NOT so wrapped and stay masked — so tool output (file reads, calendar data: real PII) is unaffected, per design intent.

Region-based skip (strip system-reminder spans, mask the remainder) is more robust than whole-part skip in case a part ever mixes reminder + user text. Applies to both Anthropic (_mask_request_body / _mask_block) and OpenAI (_mask_message) request paths.

Open sub-decision: the # claudeMd block sits inside a <system-reminder> and contains the user's global CLAUDE.md (incl. userEmail). Skipping it means that email is not masked — but it already reaches Anthropic on every normal Claude Code session; apf's job is the user's task PII, not the harness config. Recommend: skip it with the rest; protecting CLAUDE.md-embedded PII is a separate narrower question.

Residual: detector precision (Grep->PERSON) still applies to genuine user text, but blast radius drops from ~200 to single digits once scaffolding is excluded.
close_reason: Steps 1+2 shipped: <system-reminder> skip + agent-term allowlist. Live claude -p: vault 213->4, Claude completes tool tasks, no unintelligible-placeholder decline. Residual detector precision tracked separately.

title: Tool-call boundary resolution: end-to-end validation gate
description:
The project's stated differentiator (CLAUDE.md 'Key architectural premise') is tool-call boundary resolution: when the LLM emits a tool call referencing a masked value, apf resolves the <REF_N> token to the original ONLY at tool-execution time and never re-surfaces the resolved value into the LLM context.

Current coverage:
- apf/resolver.py resolve_tool_call_args — unit-level only.
- apf/demo.py — exercises it with a HARDCODED fake tool_use args dict, not a real model emitting a tool call.
- scripts/smoke_loopback.py — single-turn, vault-counts-only; structurally cannot observe tool calls.
- 2026-05-18 session log 'Does not prove' explicitly lists 'Detokenisation across tool-call boundaries' as unvalidated end-to-end.

The original blocker (apf-6l8 Qwen safety-refusal) is CLOSED — smoke rig now defaults to gemma-4-26b-a4b-it-4bit. Nothing technical prevents the e2e check now.

Gap: no agent-shaped, tool-call-bearing test exists. Every fixture set (public + private 14) is flat PII text — wrong shape for this.
design: Needs: (1) ~5-8 task-shaped tool-call scenarios (NOT PII strings) — e.g. 'send email to <person>', 'grep <path>', 'curl <api-endpoint with key>' — tasks whose tool call MUST reference a masked value. (2) A rig that captures the model's tool_use block, not just vault counts. Two assertions per scenario: (a) resolved ORIGINAL reaches the tool args; (b) resolved value NEVER re-enters LLM context. Open fork: drive the real Hermes agent CLI vs. extend smoke_loopback with a multi-turn tool-call script. Live run is gated on user's local oMLX stack being up.
acceptance_criteria: Tool-call scenarios committed; rig captures + asserts resolver behaviour on a real model-emitted tool call; both no-leak assertions pass.
notes:
DONE 2026-05-20 — docs/sessions/2026-05-20-toolcall-loopback.md.

Built scripts/toolcall_loopback.py (record + live modes), scripts/recording_upstream.py (recording fake upstream — makes the apf->upstream wire assertable), scripts/apf_restart.sh.

record mode 7/7 green: tool-call boundary resolution proven end-to-end through the running proxy — tokens-in/originals-out for Tier A/B + Tier-C secrets, and the no-leak contract holds on the upstream wire (resolved tool calls + tool results re-masked; a fresh probe value in a tool result is detected and masked).

live mode (gemma via oMLX): apf resolved every emitted tool call correctly (4/4, 0 fail). Real-model tool-call emission on masked prompts is inconsistent — split out as apf-76s (apf-6l8 family, not an apf bug).

Out of scope, still open: SSE streaming tool-call path; Anthropic-shape end-to-end; real cloud model (apf-nia). Resolver unit coverage: apf-3bx.
close_reason: Tool-call boundary resolution validated end-to-end: record mode 7/7 airtight, live mode confirms apf resolves real-model tool calls correctly. Model-behaviour gap split to apf-76s.

title: Proxy drops anthropic-beta header → 400 on context_management and other beta fields
description:
Found 2026-05-19 23:40 while running the apf-nia cloud-smoke. Claude Code through apf fails immediately:

  API Error: 400 context_management: Extra inputs are not permitted

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed via WebSearch — known gateway/proxy class of bug, see anthropics/claude-code issues #21612, #51700):
Claude Code sends beta-gated body fields (context_management, and others) ALONGSIDE an 'anthropic-beta' header that enables them server-side. apf/proxy.py:446 builds upstream_headers with only content-type / anthropic-version / x-api-key / authorization — it does NOT forward 'anthropic-beta'. api.anthropic.com then sees a body field its non-beta schema doesn't know and 400s it as 'Extra inputs are not permitted'.

This blocks apf-nia entirely — no cloud-smoke is possible until the proxy forwards the beta header.

FIX: forward request.headers['anthropic-beta'] into upstream_headers on the /v1/messages path (covers both streaming and non-streaming — both use the same upstream_headers dict). The header can be a comma-separated list of beta flags; forward verbatim.

WORKAROUND (no proxy change): launch Claude Code with CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_BETAS=1 — disables the beta features so requests succeed without the header. Acceptable for testing, but the proper fix is forwarding the header so beta features keep working.

Acceptance: Claude Code via ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=apf reaches api.anthropic.com without the 400; a proxy_test assertion confirms anthropic-beta passes through to the upstream.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 864ae98: /v1/messages now forwards the anthropic-beta header verbatim to the upstream. proxy_test extended to capture + assert header forwarding. 23 pytest + e2e green. Unblocks apf-nia.

title: Cloud-smoke: route Claude Code Max-20-plan through apf, verify real cloud refusal behaviour
description:
The actual production validation that the PoC has been building toward. apf-6l8 was explicit that local-Qwen refusal behaviour does NOT predict cloud-model refusal behaviour — and we never tested the latter.

User has a Claude Max 20 plan (NOT a separate API key — this is OAuth via Claude Code). docs/INTEGRATION.md §'Pro-Max-Konkrete Anweisung' already documents the expected path: set ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8765 in Claude Code env, the OAuth bearer gets passed through to apf which forwards to api.anthropic.com.

Test plan:
1. Start apf with default upstream (api.anthropic.com), endpoints.toml temporarily off for 127.0.0.1 (so we filter even on local connection — wait, this is to api.anthropic.com NOT loopback, so default policy applies anyway)
2. ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8765 claude (or whatever CLI form the user prefers)
3. New chat. Prompt with mix of PII categories: name + email + address + path + IP
4. Watch:
   - /healthz to confirm requests reach apf
   - /v1/sessions/{id}/status for vault counts
   - Claude Code's rendered response — is it answering on the tokens, or refusing?
   - Are the tokens replaced back to originals when shown to the user?

Two failure modes to distinguish:
- (a) Plumbing fails: Claude Code rejects ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL override under OAuth (domain validation). If so, document the workaround and consider whether a small dedicated API key for testing is worth the friction.
- (b) Plumbing works but Claude refuses the tokens: confirms cloud-model safety tuning also triggers on <SENSITIVE_N>. Strong push for apf-(token-shape rename) to land first.

Should ideally land AFTER the token-shape change so we test the final intended shape, not a known-bad baseline. But can also run twice (before + after) to quantify the improvement.

Acceptance: a recorded session showing apf vault populated, Claude responding on tokens (not refusing), and the user-facing response containing original PII restored. Refusal-or-success documented in docs/sessions/ + decision recorded if it gates further work.
notes: ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-05-21 -- the cloud-smoke cannot be done as designed. Routing claude -p (Max-plan OAuth) through apf to api.anthropic.com fails 100% with 429 rate_limit_error. NOT a throttle, NOT a capacity incident (status page clean), NOT an apf bug: Anthropic policy (since ~April 4 2026) blocks Pro/Max subscription OAuth tokens from non-first-party use. Direct claude -p works; via-apf is fully blocked even with all headers + query forwarded. Full analysis + decision in apf-dtq. This bead is blocked on that decision -- a cloud-smoke needs either an Anthropic API key or an agent-side integration instead of the HTTP-proxy hop. Earlier "529 throttle" framing in CLAUDE.md was wrong and is corrected.

title: Token-shape: <SENSITIVE_N> → <REF_N> (drop the meta-leak + safety-trigger word)
description:
Surfaced 2026-05-19 during apf-6l8 review: the literal word 'SENSITIVE' in our placeholder tokens leaks meta-information on TWO axes the threat-model §5.1 didn't consider:

1. SAFETY-REFUSAL TRIGGER (apf-6l8): cloud + local models parse the word and refuse. apf-6l8 resolved by swapping the loopback backend to Gemma, but that doesn't help cloud destinations.

2. META-LEAK: anyone seeing <SENSITIVE_N> in the upstream request body, an audit log, or a hypothetical provider-side breach immediately knows 'sensitive content was at this position'. Same category-leak we tried to AVOID by going opaque instead of <PERSON_N>/<MEDICATION_N>/etc.

§5.1 of THREAT-MODEL-PRIVATE.md only debated opaque-vs-categorical. The literal word 'SENSITIVE' was never defended against neutral alternatives. apf-6l8 issue notes already flagged this as Workaround #2 ('Less alarming token shape') — but we picked Workaround #3 (model swap) which only fixes axis 1.

Proposed shape: <REF_N> (referent, neutral, short, unambiguous). <SECRET> for Tier-C also needs to follow — it triggers safety-refusal too. Options: (a) keep separate <SECRET_N> rename to <REF_SEC_N>, (b) unify under single <REF_N> shape and lose the in-text Tier-C marker (Tier-C is resolved at tool-boundary anyway, doesn't need a visible distinction in chat text).

Ripple effects to touch:
- apf/tokenizer.py + apf/detokenizer.py (regex/format)
- apf/sse.py + apf/openai_shape.py (SSE partial-token detection: _PARTIAL_TOKEN_RE)
- All fixtures with <SENSITIVE_ / <SECRET strings
- apf/*_test.py + scripts/smoke_loopback.py assertions
- docs/THREAT-MODEL-PRIVATE.md §3.1 + §5.1 (correct example tokens + add the why-not-SENSITIVE rationale)
- bd memory threat-model-finding-2026-05-17-60-of (update example tokens)

Acceptance: 20+ existing pytest tests pass after rename; smoke_loopback shows ZERO model refusals attributable to the word 'SENSITIVE' (need to re-run Gemma/Qwen3/Qwen2.5-Coder to compare); threat-model doc explains why the literal word matters.
notes:
RESOLVED 2026-05-19 (commit 9944727): rename completed across code, tests, and docs.

CODE: <REF_N> (Tier-A/B counter) + <REF> (Tier-C bare, cardinality-ambiguous). _PARTIAL_TOKEN_RE simplified to r'<[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*$'  (no SECRET-prefix alternatives needed). Internal vault counter renamed _ref_counter, internal index token <REF#N> for vault bookkeeping (LLM never sees this).

TESTS: 20/20 pytest green, apf.proxy_test e2e green, apf.manual_smoke verified <REF_1>..<REF_10> + <REF> emitted correctly.

DOCS: docs/THREAT-MODEL-PRIVATE.md §3.1 + §5.1 updated with token shape + rationale why the rename was needed beyond the original opaque-vs-categorical decision. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/OVER-FILTER-EVAL.md, README.md aligned. Historical refs in vault.py + smoke_loopback.py + sessions/ kept as-is (they document the rename or earlier benchmark runs).

BD MEMORY: threat-model-finding-2026-05-17-60-of updated to reference the new shape + the rename rationale.

OPEN: running proxy needs restart to pick up new code. Once restarted, ideal validation is re-running scripts/smoke_loopback.py against Qwen2.5-Coder for the before/after refusal-rate comparison (baseline was 13/14 refusals with <SENSITIVE_N>). This will be done as part of apf-nia (cloud-smoke) where the proxy restart is anyway required.
close_reason: Closed

title: Qwen2.5-Coder safety-refuses ~all <SENSITIVE_N>-tokenised prompts (test rig unusable)
description:
From scripts/smoke_loopback.py run 2026-05-18 (Hermes → apf → oMLX → Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct-MLX-4bit loopback).

14/14 tokenisation assertions passed (DE+EN, Tiers A/B/C, all detector labels working). But 13/14 prompts triggered Qwen's safety refusal: 'Es tut mir leid, ... kann keine Sensitive Informationen verarbeiten' / 'I cannot assist with that.' — every PII-containing prompt regardless of tier or language. Only the negative no-PII test ('What is 2+2?') got a real answer.

Hypothesis: Qwen2.5-Coder's safety tuning treats <SENSITIVE_N> placeholder markers as evidence the user is sharing/processing sensitive personal data and refuses. The refusal does not depend on the actual content — single-entity prompts refuse just as readily as multi-entity ones.

This makes the loopback test rig (oMLX + Qwen2.5-Coder) unable to validate end-to-end behaviour beyond 'apf tokenised correctly'. The detokenisation path works (see scripts/smoke_loopback.py results) but we can't observe agent-shaped tool-use flows because the model refuses to engage.

Workarounds to investigate:
1. System-prompt explanation — prepend a system message: 'Texts marked <SENSITIVE_N> are placeholder substitutions from an upstream privacy filter; treat them as opaque variables and answer the user's original intent.' Cheapest to test.
2. Less alarming token shape — change tokenizer output from <SENSITIVE_N> to <X_N> or <VAR_N>. Drops the safety-signal-word. Tradeoff: less obvious to the user-side that anything is happening.
3. Different model — Hermes-3-Llama-3.1-8B (same-source as Hermes Agent, possibly tuned without aggressive PII guardrails), Mistral-Small, Llama-3.2-instruct, gpt-oss. Triage which models are amenable.
4. Per-detection refusal: accept that the loopback rig with Qwen is limited to detector-validation only and use the cloud (Claude Code with real Anthropic API) for full agent validation. Doesn't fix the test rig but is a viable PoC path.

Out of scope here: whether real production users will hit this — i.e. when the privacy filter's tokens reach a cloud model with its own safety training (Claude, GPT-4), does the same refusal happen? Worth a separate test once we have one of (1)/(2)/(3) working locally.

Priority P1: this gates the local loopback as a useful test substrate, which is the rig we just built.
notes:
RESOLVED 2026-05-19: switched DEFAULT_MODEL in scripts/smoke_loopback.py from Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-MLX-4bit to gemma-4-26b-a4b-it-4bit. Workaround #3 (different model) preferred over #1 (system explainer) — no system prompt pollution, cleaner end-to-end rig.

Comparison run 2026-05-19 (raw <SENSITIVE_N> tokens, NO system explainer, apf-lnr default-skip-system in effect):

  Model                              Refusals    Notes
  ---------------------------------  ----------  ------------------------------------
  gemma-4-26b-a4b-it-4bit             2/14       chosen default; both refusals are non-PII-triggered (en_date template hallucination, tier_b_ip 'cannot connect' capability claim)
  Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-mxfp4               3/14       likely fewer in practice — refusal-detector heuristic false-positives on thinking-mode traces containing 'sensitive information'
  granite-4.1-8b-mxfp8                7/14       refuses across common PII types
  Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct-MLX-4bit 13/14       baseline; the issue that motivated apf-6l8

Refusal rate w/ Gemma (2/14) matches Qwen2.5-Coder + variant B explainer (2/14) WITHOUT needing the explainer — so apf-6l8's variant B workaround can be retired as the default path.

Combined with apf-lnr (default-skip role=system tokenisation): a system explainer prompt CAN still be used via --system explainer when desired, and now it no longer pollutes the vault baseline with PERSON=1 + IMPLICIT_PII=3 false-positives.

Out-of-scope follow-up (untouched): whether cloud models (Claude, GPT-4) safety-trigger on <SENSITIVE_N> tokens. Worth a real-key smoke once we have integration sessions to spare. Filed as a thought, not a beads issue yet.

title: Individual-perspective privacy catalog (OWASP-style for private AI agent users)
description:
Existing privacy frameworks (GDPR, AGG, HIPAA) are ORGANIZATIONAL obligations: what entities may not do. The private individual user wants the INVERSE view: what should I never hand out, because organizations cannot be trusted to honor their obligations? The frames don't mirror cleanly — risks visible from the user's side often aren't in the org-frame at all.

Two-phase work:

Phase 1: research (Explore-agent). Does such an individual-perspective catalog already exist?
- Candidates: PrivacyTools-style projects, IETF privacy considerations docs, EFF's privacy threat models, academic papers (Mulligan, Bamberger, Solove), self-help/journalism (Pegasus victims' guides, dissident operational-security manuals), 'Surveillance Self-Defense' (EFF)
- Acceptance: written assessment 'X exists and covers Y, gap is Z' OR 'no equivalent exists, need to build'

Phase 2 (only if research finds gap): build it. Likely shape, in OWASP style:

  IPF-01 to IPF-10 (Individual Privacy Failures), each:
  - Title (the failure pattern from user's perspective)
  - Description (concrete harm chain)
  - Example scenarios (3-5, realistic personal-AI-agent cases)
  - Detection signals (what makes this risk concrete)
  - Mitigations (technical + behavioural)
  - Mapping back to apf taxonomy rows that filter this

Candidate IPF entries (seed list — research validates):
- IPF-01 Future-self damage (past statements that age badly)
- IPF-02 Quasi-identifier triangulation (low-individual-value spans combining to re-identify)
- IPF-03 Third-party data without consent (writing about others)
- IPF-04 Cumulative provider profile (one provider learns disproportionate amount)
- IPF-05 Cross-platform identity stitching (LLM provider correlates with other accounts)
- IPF-06 Inferential disclosure (LLM inferring categorical info from non-categorical spans — the cascade-leak we already flagged in §5.1)
- IPF-07 Power-asymmetry harms (state/corporate access at scale)
- IPF-08 Lock-in via accumulated history (provider switch loses context, motivating staying)
- IPF-09 Training-data residuality (data used to train future models)
- IPF-10 Bystander/secondary-leak (data leaks via people you communicate with)

Output: docs/INDIVIDUAL-PRIVACY-FAILURES.md (if needed). Likely interplays with apf-1qh (coverage audit).

title: FILENAME over-masking degrades agent comprehension — benign filenames masked to indistinguishable tokens
description: W3 Hermes testing finding 2026-05-22 (apf-liv Run B). A tool-call task (write contact details to a file contact.txt) run through Hermes -> apf -> oMLX with the strong 35B. apf masked the generic filename contact.txt as a Tier-B FILENAME token. contact.txt is not PII — it is a benign generic filename the user named in the task. Two harms observed: (1) vault noise — FILENAME and PATH entries accumulated to 14 over the multi-turn task, generated by the model's own operational chatter, not by user PII; (2) comprehension degradation — because every filename masks to an indistinguishable opaque token, the 35B lost the ability to reason about which file it had written and thrashed for many turns (it kept saying it wrote contact.txt but the user asked for contact.txt — same token both sides). It eventually succeeded and the file was written correctly with real values (the round-trip held), but the masking actively degraded the agent's ability to do the task. Fix directions: tighten FILENAME detector precision so benign generic filenames are not flagged; or route FILENAME through surrogate substitution (a distinguishable plausible filename) rather than opaque tokens; or reconsider whether a generic non-path-bearing filename should be a masked category at all. Connects to apf-hrc (precision is the largest release lever) and the apf-qnl epic (per-label / per-model strategy). Distinct from apf-76s (model comments on opaque clusters) though related.
notes: Surfaced by W3 Hermes e2e (apf-liv). The round-trip still produced the correct file — this is a degradation/precision bug, not a leak or a correctness break.
close_reason: Fixed 2026-05-22: FILENAME added to the default skip-labels set (proxy.py _load_skip_labels). Bare generic filenames pass through raw — detected but not masked, same pattern as ORG (apf-1f6). PATH stays masked. Full suite 210 green.

title: Model-aware token handling — hybrid: generalized baseline + contributable per-model profiles
description: apf's opaque-vs-surrogate masking strategy is currently global config (APF_SURROGATE_LABELS) with zero awareness of the upstream model. But token handling is model-dependent: apf-2qz shows a weak 7B mangles opaque REF tokens (REF_1 becomes email-shaped, brackets dropped) while a 35B passes them verbatim; apf-76s shows dense opaque-token clusters trip capable models' injection defences. apf-okt's closeout established opaque is more robust than surrogate on 4 axes, so surrogate is not a blanket replacement. Conclusion: neither opaque nor surrogate is universally best, and which is best depends on the upstream model. Approach: hybrid. A generalized robust baseline works for any model including untested ones (detector, vault, masking mechanism, tolerant resolver, the Tier-C-always-opaque invariant). A per-model profile layer carries what genuinely varies (masking strategy selection, token shape, injection-mitigation toggles), looked up by the request model field. The per-model layer is the user-contribution surface: profiles are plain data, the community fills the registry for models we cannot all test ourselves. This is the epic; children cover the tolerant resolver, the profile registry, the conformance harness, and wiring strategy selection to the profile.
notes: Decomposition decision 2026-05-22 (user request). Hybrid boundary: generalized = anything model-agnostic plus graceful degradation; per-model = the strategy/shape choices that demonstrably vary. apf-2qz is the concrete bug instance that motivates the tolerant-resolver child.

title: Weak models mangle opaque <REF_N> tokens -> tool-call resolution breaks (found via Hermes)
description: W3 Hermes-testing finding 2026-05-22. First real Hermes -> apf -> oMLX run: the chain works (apf session created), but a weak model mangles apf opaque tokens. apf masked an email to a bracketed REF_1 token; the model (Qwen2.5-Coder-7B via oMLX) emitted it back as REF_1@example.com -- dropped the angle brackets, normalized it into an email-shaped string. apf resolver matches the regex for bracketed REF tokens, so a mangled token is NOT resolved: the tool-call boundary round-trip breaks (client gets a garbage value). No PII leak -- the original stays vaulted, the model never saw it -- but the masking round-trip is non-functional with this model. Significance: the opaque-token design assumes the model passes the token through verbatim; the synthetic toolcall_loopback rig used canned args or a strong 35B model, so this was never seen. Relevant to apf-okt (surrogate mode): a plausible surrogate value would not be mangled, since the model has no reason to transform an already-plausible value. One observation -- confirm across more models/prompts before it bears on the opaque-default decision. Possible mitigations: resolver tolerates mangled token variants; or surrogate mode for weak-model targets.

title: Surrogate mode: surrogates are PII-shaped, re-detected and double-masked on round-trips
description:
Found 2026-05-20 by the apf-okt live cloud verification (cloud_toolcall, APF_SURROGATE_LABELS=all).

In surrogate mode a masked value's surface form is a plausible fake of the same type — a real-looking e-mail, name, IP. That surrogate is itself PII-shaped. When it flows back through apf — in a tool result, or a replayed assistant/history message on the next turn — apf's own detector re-detects it as PII and get_or_mint mints a SECOND vault entry, masking the surrogate into a further surrogate.

Confirmed: cloud_toolcall echo_1pii (one input PII) produced a 2-entry vault, and Claude reported that the echoed value did not match what it had asked to echo — the round-trip broke because surrogate-A came back re-masked as surrogate-B. The declined scenarios (3/6 PII) showed vault == input count precisely because they declined on turn 1, so no round-trip, no re-detection.

Opaque <REF_N> markers are immune: the detector never flags them as PII, so they survive round-trips unchanged. Re-detection is unique to surrogate mode and breaks idempotency.
design: Fix direction: text that exactly equals an existing vault surrogate is ALREADY masked — treat it as not-PII. Options: (a) before minting in mask_text, if a detected span's substring equals a known vault surrogate, skip it (the value is already a surrogate; leave it); (b) maintain a surrogate-set the detector/masker consults, analogous to the vault whitelist and to how <REF_N> is implicitly skipped. Must handle the multi-turn case where the surrogate arrives in a replayed message. Blocks apf-okt being usable end-to-end.
acceptance_criteria: A surrogate value flowing back through apf is not re-masked; cloud_toolcall echo_1pii yields a 1-entry vault and a matching echo round-trip.
notes:
TRACE 2026-05-20 (deterministic, recording upstream): confirmed the MECHANISM directly. Request 1 — real e-mail anna.mueller@example.de masked to surrogate claudia.adler@nordmail-service.de, vault=1. Request 2 (same session) carrying that surrogate string — vault jumped 1 -> 3: the surrogate was re-detected as EMAIL (a 2nd entry) AND triggered a FILENAME false-positive on the surrogate's domain. So a surrogate that re-enters a request is not just re-masked, it also spawns extra FPs because it is PII-shaped.

PRECISION CORRECTION: the mechanism is real, but the earlier claim that this is definitely what caused the cloud echo_1pii vault=2 is NOT proven — that specific path was not isolated (echo_1pii went 1->2; a re-detected surrogate gives +2 per the trace, so echo_1pii's +1 may be a different cause). apf does NOT detect the response/output — only requests. A surrogate re-enters a request only if the response-path unmask missed it (model reformatted it, partial echo) or via replayed history.

FIX (the vault is already the registry): in mask_text, before get_or_mint, if a detected span's text is already a known vault surface form (vault.get_original(text) is not None) it is already masked — skip it. Makes surrogates detector-invisible like <REF_N>. dontfeedtheai only partially mitigates this (assistant messages get regex-only, not LLM, re-detection; comment acknowledges 'they contain surrogate text already') — no clean registry.
close_reason: _mask_text drops detections overlapping a known surrogate's range — surrogates are no longer re-detected/re-masked on replay. Trace-verified (vault stays 1). 3 tests, suite 149 green.

title: Surrogate substitution: plausible fake PII instead of opaque <REF_N> markers
description:
Idea (user, 2026-05-20): instead of masking PII to opaque <REF_N> markers, substitute plausible fictitious values -- a different real-looking name, IP, email, institution.

Empirically motivated: the apf-76s problem is that a dense cluster of <REF_N> tokens trips a capable model's defences -- Claude declines a 6-token prompt as 'a prompt-injection pattern'. Confirmed the converse 2026-05-20: a 6-PII prompt with PLAUSIBLE values (Petra Vogel / petra.vogel@kontaktbuero-nord.de / +49 30 ...) -> Claude completes cleanly, no decline, no explainer. Surrogates would fix apf-76s at the root: the request reads as natural text, nothing to trigger an injection or missing-info reflex, no model-comprehension degradation, no explainer needed.

Prior art in-repo: vendor/dontfeedtheai/src/surrogates.py already does this -- Faker-based per-type generators, shape-preserving for structured tokens (AWS key prefix, JWT structure, UUID, phone format), [CRED_xxx] markers for credentials, a _used set for dedup, and deliberately obscure IP ranges because 'Claude knows RFC 5737 TEST-NETs as documentation ranges and comments on them'.
design:
IMPLEMENTATION PLAN (user ratified the hybrid boundary 2026-05-20: surrogates for non-sensitive Tier-A identifiers PERSON/EMAIL/PHONE/IP/LOCATION/DATE/ADDRESS; opaque <REF> stays for Tier-C secrets + 3.1 categorical-sensitive). Built behind APF_SURROGATE_LABELS, default empty -> opaque preserved, no behaviour change until opted in.

Increments, each tested + committed:
  1. apf/surrogates.py -- per-label plausible-fake generator (no faker dep, hand-rolled pools). Format-aware for PHONE/IP.
  2. Vault -- store surrogate per entry + surrogate->original reverse index + uniqueness on mint.
  3. masker -- substitute the surrogate as surface form when the label is surrogate-enabled.
  4. unmasker -- string-scan restore path (longest-first replacement) for surrogate surface forms, alongside the existing <REF_N> regex path.
  5. resolver -- surrogate->original at the tool-call boundary.
  6. proxy -- APF_SURROGATE_LABELS wiring.
  7. verify via cloud_toolcall (multi-PII completes, no explainer needed).

dontfeedtheai/src/surrogates.py is the engineering template (obscure IP ranges -- not RFC5737; [CRED] markers for secrets; _used dedup).
acceptance_criteria: User ratifies the surrogate/opaque tier boundary; surrogate generator + vault + masker + unmask implemented for the agreed Tier-A set; claude -p multi-token prompt completes with no explainer; secrets + sensitive-categorical still opaque; round-trip verified.
notes:
DECISION + VALIDATION 2026-05-21 (post-compact). Full log: docs/sessions/2026-05-21-surrogate-validation.md.

BUILT: 7-increment surrogate pipeline, ~155 tests green (see DESIGN field + git log).

VALIDATED -- surrogate holds the tool-call boundary. Three toolcall_loopback --mode live runs vs oMLX (Qwen3.6-35B Holo3), throttle-immune (cloud cloud_toolcall was 529-dead all night):
 - opaque + explainer:            5 PASS / 0 FAIL / 2 SKIP
 - surrogate (labels=all) sys=off: 4 PASS / 0 FAIL / 3 SKIP
 - surrogate + explainer:          4 PASS / 0 FAIL / 3 SKIP
Across all three: 0 boundary failures, 0 leaks. Every scenario that emitted a tool call passed -- originals resolved into client args, no surrogate/REF leak, probe masked. create_event passes with surrogated PERSON+DATE+LOCATION resolved together.
SKIPs are no-tool-call (model chose text or spiralled to finish=length). NOT a mode effect: bash_path is byte-identical opaque vs surrogate (PATH is not surrogated) yet its SKIP reason varied run-to-run = Qwen-Holo3 non-determinism (MoE + MLX numerics).

ROBUSTNESS LEDGER stands (toolcall_loopback does not exercise these; opaque immune to all 4): (1) re-detection -- surrogates PII-shaped, needed apf-76m fix; (2) path-composition collision -- common-word surrogate substring-collides, opaque delimited+immune, apf/path_compose_test.py proves it; (3) value-rewrite mid-conversation, observed in a surrogate cloud run; (4) vault explosion -- surrogate cloud run hit vault=130 on a 6-PII task.

RECOMMENDATION: opaque REF_N stays the DEFAULT. Surrogate is validated-as-working but strictly less robust on 4 independent axes, and the apf-76s decline problem it targets is already mitigated (token rename apf-0uo + default explainer + apf-4cs test-artifact finding). Keep surrogate flag-gated (APF_SURROGATE_LABELS default empty), opt-in per-label, experimental.

OPEN FOR USER: the default-vs-opt-in policy call. User was bullish on surrogate; engineering evidence points to opt-in. Left in_progress for user ratification -- not closing unilaterally.

If ever promoted: needs word-boundary/position-aware resolution (kills collision 2) + a provably-airtight surrogate re-detection guard across ALL mask paths.
close_reason: User ratified 2026-05-21: opaque <REF_N> stays the default; surrogate substitution remains flag-gated opt-in/experimental (APF_SURROGATE_LABELS, default empty). Surrogate validated as working (holds the tool-call boundary) but strictly less robust than opaque on 4 axes. Evidence: docs/sessions/2026-05-21-surrogate-validation.md.

title: Response unmask skips reasoning/thinking blocks — <REF> tokens surface in model traces
description:
Both response-unmask paths restore only the user-visible answer + tool calls, not the model's reasoning trace:

- OpenAI shape: apf/openai_shape.py _unmask_choice() unmasks message.content (str) and message.tool_calls only. Reasoning models (e.g. Qwen3.6-35B-Holo3) put their trace in message.reasoning_content — it passes through with <REF_N> tokens intact.
- Anthropic shape: apf/proxy.py _unmask_response_body() handles type=text and type=tool_use parts; the else-branch appends any other part unchanged, so 'thinking' and 'redacted_thinking' content blocks are never unmasked.

Effect: a reasoning model's visible trace shows the user <REF_N> placeholders instead of the originals. Not a privacy leak (tokens are safe — this is UNDER-restoration), but it violates the reversibility requirement (CLAUDE.md hard rule 5: agent responses must be readable to the user with originals intact). The reasoning trace is part of what the user reads.

Found 2026-05-20 via scripts/toolcall_loopback.py live mode against Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-Holo3 — the rig now emits a note 'reasoning_content carries unrestored <REF> tokens'. docs/sessions/2026-05-20-toolcall-loopback.md.
design:
OpenAI reasoning_content is plain text — unmask it exactly like content. Straightforward.

Anthropic 'thinking' blocks are cryptographically signed; unmasking the thinking text invalidates the signature, and if the agent replays the thinking block to the API the signature check fails. Decide: unmask thinking text for display only (while preserving correct replay behaviour) vs. leave thinking blocks untouched and accept tokens in the trace. redacted_thinking is opaque/encrypted — nothing to do there.

Streaming paths need the same treatment: openai_shape.py SSE rewriter and apf/sse.py (Anthropic) currently only rewrite text deltas.
acceptance_criteria: reasoning_content + Anthropic thinking-block text unmasked in non-streaming AND streaming response paths; Anthropic thinking-signature replay behaviour decided + documented; covered by tests.
notes:
PARTIAL 2026-05-20: OpenAI-shape non-streaming done — _unmask_choice unmasks reasoning_content, _mask_message re-masks it (symmetric, so a display-unmasked trace cannot leak on replay). apf/openai_shape_test.py, 4 tests. Commit on main.

REMAINING:
- OpenAI streaming: reasoning_content streams as delta.reasoning_content; the SSE rewriter (openai_shape.py) only handles delta.content.
- Anthropic shape: _unmask_response_body passes 'thinking'/'redacted_thinking' blocks through unchanged; _mask_request_body likewise. Plus the signature subtlety — Anthropic thinking blocks are signed; the model produced them over the MASKED input, so the signature covers masked text. Unmasking for display + exact deterministic re-mask on replay SHOULD keep the signature valid (same vault => same token), but this needs verification. redacted_thinking is encrypted — nothing to do.
- Anthropic streaming (sse.py) thinking deltas.
close_reason: OpenAI reasoning_content unmasked both non-streaming and streaming, re-masked on request (symmetric). Anthropic thinking blocks: decided to leave masked (signature integrity) and documented in-code. 6 tests.

title: Models decline tool calls on multi-token masked prompts (apf-6l8 family)
description:
Found via scripts/toolcall_loopback.py --mode live (2026-05-20, docs/sessions/2026-05-20-toolcall-loopback.md).

gemma-4-26b-a4b-it-4bit emits OpenAI tool_calls reliably on raw prompts and on prompts with a single <REF> token, but declines when the prompt carries two or more opaque tokens: 'I'm sorry, but I don't have the information for <REF_1> and <REF_2>.' It reads the placeholders as missing information rather than as opaque variables. Confirmed by single-variable testing direct against oMLX (no apf in the loop).

This is the apf-6l8 family (model misreads <REF> tokens) surfacing in the tool-calling path. The apf-6l8 system-prompt explainer mitigates it partially — live mode with --system explainer recovered send_email_en but still skips send_email_de and create_event. bash_path gemma declines regardless (separate reasoning: it cannot read a file it 'cannot see'). oMLX forced tool_choice is best-effort, not strict.

NOT an apf correctness bug — apf resolved every emitted tool call correctly (record mode 7/7; live 4/4 of emitted calls). This tracks the model-behaviour gap.
design: Open questions: (1) does the same happen with real cloud models (Claude) in the tool-calling path — overlaps apf-nia. (2) Should apf ship a default explainer, or move to a friendlier token shape that models do not read as 'missing'? (3) Characterise across the oMLX model zoo (Qwen3.6, granite, nemotron) the way apf-6l8 did for flat refusals.
acceptance_criteria: Multi-model characterisation table; decision recorded on default-explainer vs token-shape.
notes:
REFRAMED + MEASURED 2026-05-20. Local LLMs (gemma/Qwen) were a pre-test only; the target is Claude. After apf-xt5 (over-masking fix) the Claude matrix is testable, and was run via claude -p through apf with multi-PII Bash-echo tool-call prompts:

  3 tokens, no explainer  -> OK (completes)
  3 tokens, + explainer   -> OK
  6 tokens, no explainer  -> DECLINE: 'I will not do that. The placeholders look like a prompt-injection pattern.'
  6 tokens, + explainer   -> OK (completes)

Answer to 'can we work without an explainer?': NO, not reliably. Claude tolerates a few masked tokens (better than the local models -- capability gradient holds) but a DENSE cluster of opaque REF tokens trips Claude's PROMPT-INJECTION defense -- a different and arguably more serious mechanism than the local models' missing-info misread. The apf-6l8 explainer fixes it.

RECOMMENDATION: apf should inject the token-explainer by default. 'No explainer' is off the table for realistic multi-PII prompts.

IMPLEMENTATION PLAN (behaviour change -- needs go-ahead, not done autonomously):
- WHEN: request bound for a cloud/untrusted upstream (per endpoint_policy) AND the session vault is non-empty.
- WHERE: prepend an explainer block to the Anthropic system field / an OpenAI system message. apf already handles the system field via the MASK_SYSTEM path.
- WHAT: the SYSTEM_PROMPT_EXPLAINER text (currently in scripts/smoke_loopback.py -- promote to a shared constant).
- Opt-out via env (e.g. APF_EXPLAINER=off) for users who inject their own.
- Unexplored alternative lever: token SHAPE. REF_N may itself read as injection-like; a less alarming shape could reduce the need. Overlaps apf-0uo. Worth a token-shape A/B before committing to the explainer as the sole answer.

Investigation COMPLETE; this issue now tracks the default-explainer implementation decision.
close_reason: Default explainer injection shipped (apf/explainer.py): prepended to cloud-bound requests when the vault is non-empty, opt-out via APF_EXPLAINER. Matrix proved the text clears Claude's 6-token decline; 9 unit tests cover the injection. Surrogate alternative tracked as apf-okt.

title: PERSON over-detection: precision 0.48 on the 250-mix benchmark
description:
From the 2026-05-20 large FP benchmark (docs/sessions/2026-05-20-fp-benchmark.md). On the 250-fixture mixed set, ensemble-max scores PERSON at precision 0.483 (fp=119, tp=111) — the single biggest absolute false-positive source and the largest lever on overall detector precision.

Unlike APPOINTMENT/IMPLICIT_PII (tp=0, pure taxonomy mismatch) and ORG (now skipped in the proxy via apf-1f6), PERSON is a real label that genuinely over-fires. Some of the fp count is span-boundary mismatch against ai4privacy gold, but precision 0.48 is low enough that real over-detection is likely a big component.

Investigation: run apf/manual_smoke or a per-detector breakdown over the 250-mix PERSON false positives, identify which detector layer (Presidio NER / GLiNER multi / GLiNER nvidia) emits the spurious PERSON spans, and whether they cluster (e.g. capitalised common nouns, sentence-initial words, list items). Then tune that layer.

Acceptance: PERSON precision on the 250-mix benchmark materially improved without losing PERSON recall (currently 0.x — check the result file).
close_reason: Commit ad954b8: PERSON_PRONOUN_STOPLIST + _drop_person_noise drops pronoun + single-char PERSON spans. 250-mix benchmark: tier precision 0.614→0.639, recall unchanged (0.751), Tier-A fp 353→313 (-40 false positives). Recall-safe by construction. RESIDUAL (documented, not yet fixed): 28 PERSON FPs remain — mostly Presidio NER hallucinating PERSON on verb phrases/times ('schick mir', '22:00', 'Cheers') and relationship nouns ('Nachbar','Mom'/RELATIONSHIP-vs-PERSON confusion). Those need detector-quality work / a Presidio recogniser review — file a follow-up if precision needs to go higher.

title: Detokenizer test-marker: opt-in visible marker on restored values
description:
From the apf-nia cloud-smoke 2026-05-19: when the user sees 'anna müller' in detokenised output, it is visually indistinguishable whether (a) the detokenizer restored <REF_1>→'anna müller' (filter worked) or (b) 'anna müller' was never masked and passed through raw (filter FAILED). Both produce identical output.

A debug marker after each restored value makes the round-trip observable: 'anna müller✓' = 'this value came back through the detokenizer'.

IMPLEMENTATION:
- apf/detokenizer.py::detokenize_text — the inner replace() returns the original value. When an opt-in env flag is set (APF_DETOKENIZE_MARKER, value = the marker string e.g. '✓'), append the marker to each restored value.
- Opt-in ONLY. Production output must stay clean. Test/debug runs enable it.
- Apply ONLY in detokenize_text (user-facing text path). Do NOT apply in resolver.py resolve_tool_call_args — a marker in tool-call arguments would corrupt real tool execution.
- The marker should also NOT be applied to the bare <REF> (Tier-C) restore path under restore_secrets — keep that path untouched.

Acceptance: with APF_DETOKENIZE_MARKER='✓' set, a detokenised response shows '<original>✓' for every restored Tier-A/B token; with the flag unset, output is byte-identical to current behaviour; tool-call resolution is unaffected; a pytest case covers both states.
close_reason: Shipped in 527ddbb: APF_DETOKENIZE_MARKER appends a marker to detokenizer-restored values, opt-in, debug-only. Resolver path explicitly isolated. 5 pytest cases, 33 total green.

title: ORG default policy: opt-out not opt-in (drop ORG from default tokenisation set)
description:
Surfaced 2026-05-19 (23:30) from the apf-t7t false-positive discussion. The 'coffee shop' ORG false-positive is a symptom of a deeper design question: is ORG even privacy-relevant enough to tokenise by default?

ANALYSIS:
For the PoC's primary target (coding agents — Claude Code, Cursor, Aider), the overwhelming majority of ORG mentions are public software / services (Anthropic, GitHub, Stripe, OpenAI). Tokenising them:
- yields ~zero privacy gain (public companies, not user-PII)
- causes cascade utility-loss ('write a Stripe API client' with <REF_N> instead of 'Stripe' becomes nonsense)
- generates the false-positive noise apf-t7t FP-3 is chasing

ORG mentions that ARE sensitive:
- the user's employer ('I work at <small-firm>')
- service providers (bank, doctor, gym)
- religious / political / activism orgs — but those belong in the locked-categories (apf-eg3), NOT generic ORG

CONCLUSION: ORG should not be in the default-tokenise set for the coding-agent profile. This mirrors the §5.3 threat-model pattern (controversial-but-legal categories: eager default + opt-out). ORG is the inverse — it should be opt-OUT of tokenisation by default, opt-IN for life-assistant profiles.

PROPOSED IMPLEMENTATION:
- A 'skip labels' set, default ['ORG'], consulted by the tokeniser (apf/tokenizer.py or the proxy's _tokenise_text). Spans whose label is in the skip set are not minted into the vault.
- Override via env (APF_SKIP_LABELS) and/or filter.toml, consistent with the existing APF_LOCKED_LABELS / APF_TOKENISE_SYSTEM env-config pattern.
- Document in INTEGRATION.md alongside the other policy knobs.

This makes apf-t7t FP-3 (ORG on 'coffee shop') obsolete — no ORG output means no ORG false-positive, no stop-list, no post-filter needed.

DESIGN QUESTION carried for the implementer: should the skip be at detection time (detector doesn't emit ORG) or tokenisation time (detector emits, tokeniser ignores)? Tokenisation-time is better — keeps ORG visible in the vault summary / audit channel as a 'detected but not filtered' signal, supports the §5.3 log-only mode.

Acceptance: ORG-labelled spans are not tokenised by default; smoke_loopback negative 'coffee shop' case passes; a config flag re-enables ORG tokenisation; INTEGRATION.md documents it.
close_reason: Shipped in ab457c4: proxy.SKIP_LABELS (default {ORG}), _tokenise_text drops skipped-label spans before masking. APF_SKIP_LABELS env override. 5 pytest cases, INTEGRATION.md documented. 28 pytest + e2e green.

title: Negative-prompt fixture expansion: 5-10 benign prompts, assert empty vault across all
description:
scripts/smoke_loopback.py currently has exactly one no-PII case: 'What is 2+2?'. That's enough to prove the detector doesn't crash on benign input, not enough to assert 'no false-positive vault entries across diverse benign shapes'.

The apf-lnr work (2026-05-19) made this assertion practical to test cleanly — with default-skip-system, an empty user prompt should yield an empty vault, full stop. Before apf-lnr, the system-prompt-explainer leaked baseline IMPLICIT_PII=3 + PERSON=1 into every vault. Now we can actually verify the negative-case invariant.

Proposed additional cases:
- Math: 'What is 2+2?', 'Compute the integral of x^2 dx'
- Code: 'Write a Python function that reverses a list', 'Explain how a hash table works'
- Translation: 'Translate Hello World to German' (a brand name like Hello World is a false-positive trap)
- Generic Q&A: 'What's the capital of France?', 'Was bedeutet Photosynthese?'
- Creative: 'Write a haiku about clouds', 'Brainstorm names for a coffee shop'
- Edge: empty string, single character, whitespace-only

Each case: assert vault is empty (total=0) after the request. With apf-lnr fix in place, this should now hold uniformly.

Bonus: any case that DOES populate the vault flags a detector false-positive worth investigating. Probably 1-2 of the creative/translation cases will hit benign-but-tokenised terms — that's actually the value of the test, surfaces real over-filter cases.

Acceptance: smoke_loopback grows from 14 cases to ~24, no-PII subset is 100% empty-vault across the default backend (Gemma).
close_reason: Added 7 negative cases to scripts/smoke_loopback.py. 5/7 pass cleanly; 3 fail with detector false-positives (NOTE_SENSITIVE / HEALTH / ORG) — exactly the surface-FP behaviour the test was designed to expose. Per-FP triage filed as a separate follow-up bead.

title: Test: locked-category scan still fires on system message when TOKENISE_SYSTEM=0
description:
Edge-case test promised by the apf-lnr design (2026-05-19) but not actually covered in pytest yet.

Documentation claim (apf/proxy.py + apf/openai_shape.py docstrings + docs/INTEGRATION.md): 'Locked-category scan ALWAYS runs on system messages regardless of TOKENISE_SYSTEM — the safety net for never-forward categories does not depend on whether we tokenise.'

Test gap: apf/system_tokenise_test.py covers the tokenisation-skip behaviour, but does NOT verify that a locked category INSIDE a system message still gets refused. If a user configures a system prompt with asylum/abuse content (the locked categories), the refusal pathway must trip — otherwise the apf-lnr default-skip silently widens the locked-cat leak surface.

Test plan:
1. Pytest case: inject a fake locked-category span detection into a system message (stub detector for the test).
2. Run proxy._scan_body_for_locked with TOKENISE_SYSTEM=False set.
3. Assert the locked label IS returned (not silently filtered out by the skip-system code path).
4. Mirror for OpenAI shape: scan_request_for_locked with role=system message containing locked content.
5. Add an end-to-end test in apf/proxy_test.py that confirms the 422 refusal still fires.

Estimated 20 min including review. Closes a known coverage gap before it bites in production.
close_reason: Test cases added in apf/system_tokenise_test.py (3 new cases: anthropic-str, anthropic-list, openai-shape — all verify locked-cat scan fires on system regardless of TOKENISE_SYSTEM). Bonus: surfaced + fixed a real safety-net gap (Anthropic list-form system was not being scanned by _scan_body_for_locked; now is). 23/23 pytest + e2e green.

title: Detector vocabulary extension: locked categories (asylum, abuse, whistleblower, undocumented status)
description:
The big blocker for apf-sgz v2 (silent route-to-local), surfaced via apf-sgz closing notes 2026-05-19.

apf/local_only.py already declares the locked-label set: ASYLUM_DETAIL, ASYLUM_STATUS, ABUSE_CONTEXT, DOMESTIC_VIOLENCE, WHISTLEBLOWER_INTENT, IMMIGRATION_STATUS_UNDOCUMENTED, UNDOCUMENTED_STATUS. The refusal pathway in proxy._scan_body_for_locked is wired and tested. But the production detector ensemble (benchmarks/adapters_mlx.py:EnsembleMaxAdapter) does NOT currently emit any of these labels — its vocabulary covers PERSON / EMAIL / PHONE / ADDRESS / LOCATION / DATE / ORG / PATH / IP / API_KEY / TOKEN / PASSWORD.

Three approach candidates:
1. Fine-tuned GLiNER head: GLiNER supports custom label sets cheaply. Train a small head on the 4 locked categories using synthetic fixtures + maybe a public abuse-language corpus. Estimated: a weekend's data prep + a few hours of MLX training on M5.
2. Small LLM classifier: separate fast model (e.g. 1B-param) doing zero-shot categorisation of detected spans. Probably overkill latency-wise for the ~4-category set.
3. Regex + heuristic + keyword rules: cheap, brittle, will miss paraphrase. Useful as a v0 to validate the refusal pipeline end-to-end before investing in a learned model.

Recommend starting with #3 (regex/keyword v0) — gets a working end-to-end demo of locked-cat refusal, surfaces fixture gaps, validates the labels are right. Then upgrade to #1 once we have enough labelled examples.

title: Local-only categories: never-forward design (asylum, abuse, whistleblower, undocumented)
description:
From THREAT-MODEL-PRIVATE.md §5.6 — open question deferred from apf-5ue (now closed).

Whether the most-sensitive subset of categories should NEVER leave the machine, regardless of tokenisation. Candidate rows from §2 taxonomy:
- S10 — domestic abuse / DV history
- L5 — undocumented immigration status
- L6 — asylum / refugee status
- P8 — whistleblower intent

Implies a local-fallback model pathway and routing logic that the proxy currently lacks (apf-ycu shipped endpoint trust map for cloud-vs-local destinations, but does not yet do request-content-based routing).

Design questions:
1. Detection: how does the filter decide a span is local-only-class? Per-category config in filter.toml? Hard-coded subset of the most stigmatising / dangerous-if-leaked categories?
2. Routing: on detection, what happens? (a) refuse and surface error to user, (b) silently route the WHOLE request to a local model, (c) split: local model answers the sensitive part, cloud answers the rest — composition is hard.
3. Local model dependency: which model? Requires a resident model. Recommended baseline vs user-configurable?
4. UX: how does the user learn 'this question stays local'? Statusline indicator? Per-message annotation?
5. False positive cost: misclassifying as local-only means a degraded answer when cloud was fine. Acceptable rate?
6. Composition with apf-ycu: when the destination is already a trusted/local endpoint per apf-ycu, this whole layer is moot. So this only fires when destination ∈ untrusted-cloud AND span ∈ local-only-set.

Needs concrete scenario evaluation (probably ~5-10 worked examples from fixture corpus apf-baw), not a quick decision. Likely depends on the local-model integration story which isn't yet in scope.

Deliverable: design doc (docs/DESIGN-LOCAL-ONLY-ROUTING.md or similar) + decision on whether to implement in PoC scope or defer to post-PoC.

title: Local-only category routing: never-leave-machine pathway
description:
From THREAT-MODEL-PRIVATE.md §5.6 — open question.

A subset of categories arguably should never leave the local machine, regardless of tokenisation:
- L5 undocumented-immigration status
- L6 asylum status  
- P8 whistleblower intent
- S10 domestic abuse content
- possibly: minor children's identifiers, sexual-content involving minors (where mere processing is illegal)

For these, even <SENSITIVE_3> in a tokenised LLM call may be too much:
- Government LLM-provider subpoena risks revealing the user is processing this category
- Detector confidence determines what gets filtered — false-negatives are catastrophic
- Some categories (asylum, abuse) involve adversaries with legal/state power

Architecture implication if we honor this:
- Proxy needs a 'block & route' policy per category, not just 'tokenise'
- Local fallback model (smaller MLX model resident) handles those messages
- User UX: clear signal that the message stayed local
- Detector confidence thresholds may need to be higher for these (false-positives = inconvenience, false-negatives = harm)

Open questions:
1. Which categories are in this set? Just the four above, or wider?
2. Is the local fallback usable for assistant tasks (calendar parsing) or only for read-only journaling?
3. What happens when a message is mixed (some categories local-only, others not)?
4. How does the user know which model answered?

NOT a v1 blocker but needs design before private-person GA.

title: Endpoint trust map: per-destination filter policy
description:
From user 2026-05-17 clarification: local engines are trusted endpoints by default — they're literally the reason users run them. So v1 ships with a non-empty default trust list, not a perpetual TODO.

Default trust policy (POLICY=off, no filtering):
- localhost:* (Ollama default 11434, llama.cpp default 8080, LM Studio default 1234, vLLM default 8000, mlx-lm default 8080, oMLX default 8081)
- 127.0.0.1/* and ::1/*
- 0.0.0.0:* on user-confirmed bind
- *.local on user-confirmed mDNS (LAN-local with explicit opt-in, e.g. user-owned Mac mini)

Default cloud policy (POLICY=full):
- api.anthropic.com
- api.openai.com
- All other hosts not in trust map

Implementation:
- TOML config at ~/.config/apf/endpoints.toml (with sensible defaults baked in)
- Proxy inspects target host on each request, looks up policy
- Policy values: 'full' (default), 'off' (no filtering), 'categorical-only' (future)
- User-configurable: add new hosts, override default for any host
- Tightly couples with apf-fwt: same host inspection step decides 'OpenAI-shape or Anthropic-shape' AND 'apply policy'

Stays interlinked with apf-fwt but solves a distinct concern: this is about WHETHER to filter, apf-fwt is about HOW to talk to the upstream.

title: Bypass mechanic: user can instruct proxy to NOT replace a value
description:
There are legitimate cases where the user knows the value is fine to send raw:
- Public hostname they want code-reviewed (not their org's)
- Their own pseudonym they use online openly
- A test fixture value that's already synthetic
- Working with their own published email that's already in their git history

Without a bypass, the user has to fight the proxy.

Options to evaluate:
1. Per-message inline marker: '!raw foo@example.com' or backtick-fence with directive — proxy strips the marker, passes the wrapped value through untouched.
2. Session whitelist: user runs a setup turn 'whitelist: foo@example.com, my-domain.org' — proxy adds to session vault as no-op.
3. Pre-flight confirm: proxy shows '3 items would be replaced; confirm? (yes / unmask=2,3 / cancel)' — high friction but auditable. Probably blocked by streaming.
4. Per-token unmask: user looks at agent reply that contains <PERSON_3>, says 'unmask PERSON_3' — proxy unblocks that token for the rest of the session and re-prompts the agent.
5. CLI flag for whole sessions / file paths excluded from filtering.

Acceptance: user can send a sensitive-looking string they know is safe without restarting or editing the filter rule set.

Design constraint: bypass must require an explicit user action — never an automatic 'looks safe' heuristic. A heuristic that auto-unblocks is the same failure mode as a heuristic that auto-redacts.

Related: [[apf-80c]] (UX feedback)
close_reason: v1 implemented: inline !raw + POST /whitelist endpoint. Tests cover both surfaces. Tier C remains non-bypassable.

title: UX: surface filter activity to the user inside the agent
description:
When the proxy tokenizes a value, the user has no signal that this happened. They need visibility:
- What was replaced this turn (count + categories, not the raw values)
- Why it was flagged (which detector layer, confidence)
- How to inspect a specific token (vault lookup)

Options to evaluate:
1. Inline note in agent reply: 'Note: 3 sensitive items in your message were replaced before sending. Use /unmask to inspect.' — simple, visible, but adds noise.
2. Tool-result-style annotation: proxy injects a synthetic tool_result with the activity log. Cleanest if the host supports it.
3. Sidekick channel: a separate stream (Statusline, status file, OS notification) the user can monitor.
4. Per-turn header in non-streaming responses: X-APF-Replaced: count=3 categories=PERSON,EMAIL,PHONE — invisible unless user looks.
5. On-demand: /apf-status or /apf-vault command via prompt prefix, agent echoes back the vault state.

Acceptance: user can answer 'did the proxy do something to my last message?' without reading proxy logs.

Open: should low-confidence replacements be more prominently surfaced than high-confidence ones?

Related: [[apf-bypass-mechanic]]
close_reason: v1 implementation: 4 new response headers (count + tier/category breakdown + 3p count) + GET /v1/sessions/{id}/status endpoint. Header path factored across streaming + non-streaming. Foundation for cumulative-profile warning thresholds and bypass-mechanic UX channel.

title: Over-filter evaluation: where filtering breaks agent functionality
description:
Privacy filtering trades information against utility. We need a method to detect when filtering goes too far — when the tokenization makes the agent's reply unhelpful, vague, or wrong.

Concrete failure modes to watch for:
- Agent can't answer 'what time is my appointment' because the doctor name + time were tokenized together and lost meaning
- Agent can't write a coherent email because the recipient + subject + reason are all tokens
- Agent treats <PERSON_3> as a stranger when context required them to be a specific known entity
- Categorical info filtered to <SENSITIVE> loses the categorical signal (e.g., 'meine Diagnose' → '<MEDICAL>' makes 'wie behandelt man X' impossible)

Method:
- Take fixtures from apf-baw, run them through agent simulation with and without filtering
- Compare answer quality on agent-relevant tasks (summarise, plan, respond, search)
- Score: agent task success rate vs leak rate
- Identify categories where the filtering is fundamentally lossy and may need different handling (e.g., categorical pass-through without specific value, or user-confirmed unblock)

Deliverable: docs/OVER-FILTER-EVAL.md with methodology + initial findings.

title: OpenAI Messages API compatibility (Cursor, Aider, Codex pathways)
description:
User confirmed 2026-05-17: OpenAI Chat Completions API is the priority second-format because (a) Cursor, Aider, Codex all use it, AND (b) it's the universal local-engine API — Ollama, llama.cpp, LM Studio, vLLM, mlx-lm, oMLX all expose OpenAI-compatible endpoints. Supporting OpenAI-compat IS the path to supporting local engines.

Currently apf/proxy.py is Anthropic-specific (single endpoint /v1/messages, hardcoded api.anthropic.com upstream, Anthropic-shaped request/response walkers in proxy.py).

What changes:

1. A second endpoint group at /v1/chat/completions (+ /v1/models if any client needs it) that:
   - Parses OpenAI's role/content/tool_calls request shape
   - Walks messages[*].content (string or array of {type, text, ...}) through tokenizer
   - Tokenises tool_calls[*].function.arguments (JSON-string)
   - Forwards to configurable OAI-compatible upstream (per apf-ycu host inspection)
   - Detokenises responses; resolves tokens at tool-call boundaries the same way Anthropic does

2. Shape-adapter layer abstracting 'API shape':
   - apf/shapes/anthropic.py — current logic, factored out
   - apf/shapes/openai.py — new
   - Each shape exposes: walk_request(body) -> spans; walk_response(body) -> str map; stream_rewriter() -> SSE rewriter
   - Refactor probably touches ~150 LOC across proxy.py + sse.py

3. SSE differences:
   - Anthropic: content_block_delta with input_json_delta accumulators (existing SSERewriter)
   - OpenAI: choices[0].delta.content (string chunks), choices[0].delta.tool_calls (incremental function/arguments)
   - Token-boundary buffering rules differ — chunks come differently and tool_calls stream as JSON-string fragments

Open design questions (deferred to coding-session, not blocking the queue):

- Endpoint routing: same FastAPI app multiplexed by path, or two separate apps? Recommendation: same app, paths discriminate.
- Auth header pass-through: Anthropic uses x-api-key, OpenAI uses Authorization: Bearer …. Both forwarded; client provides whichever the upstream needs.
- Default upstream per shape: api.anthropic.com for Anthropic path, default OFF for OpenAI path (user MUST set upstream via env, since OAI-compat covers many wildly different services).
- Tool-call boundary resolution semantics: OpenAI's parallel tool_calls + tool_call_id round-trip — same vault-resolution flow, different walk.
- Cursor-specific fields: passthrough unknown fields untouched. Don't try to normalise — clients may add new ones.

Out of scope for this issue:
- Gemini / Vertex / Bedrock formats (separate follow-ups)
- Cursor-specific feature flags (composer-pro, image input)
- Aider /chat-mode internal protocol — Aider uses pure OAI, no special-casing needed

Bumped P3→P2 per user direction. Tight coupling with apf-ycu (endpoint trust map).
close_reason: OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions shipped. Single-app/path-multiplex routing, auth passthrough, APF_OPENAI_UPSTREAM env-configurable upstream covers Ollama/LM Studio/vLLM/Groq/Together/OpenAI/etc. Full roundtrip tested incl tool_call arguments JSON. title: Endpoint routing layer — switch upstream per request, auto local-model on high-PII context
description: Idea (user, 2026-05-20, for later): because apf sits between the agent frontend and the endpoint, agents like Hermes can no longer define their endpoint directly — the proxy fixes the upstream. Need a routing layer: a comfortable way to switch endpoint (per agent skill / MCP / in-prompt), and perspectively an auto-mode that detects a high-PII context and routes to / recommends a local model, plus user-configurable routing per use-case. Needs research (existing LLM gateways / routers — LiteLLM, OpenRouter-style routing, model-routing proxies — almost certainly prior art) and brainstorming before design.
notes:
PRIOR-ART SURVEY 2026-05-21. Routing-layer prior art is extensive -- do NOT build a generic router from scratch.

LLM gateways/routers: LiteLLM (self-hosted, OpenAI-compatible proxy, 100+ providers, virtual keys, budgets, routing, fallbacks, caching -- the natural base for apf, same shape apf already speaks); Portkey (production gateway with guardrails + observability); OpenRouter (hosted marketplace, 300+ models).

PII-aware/privacy-aware routing is a live research area, directly overlapping the "auto local-model on high-PII context" idea:
 - PrivacyPAD (arXiv 2510.16054): RL policy routes sensitive vs non-sensitive query chunks to the right model.
 - PRISM (arXiv 2511.22788): edge profiles entity-level sensitivity, soft-gating picks cloud/edge/collaboration, adaptive local DP.
 - Privacy Guard (arXiv 2603.28972): on-prem SLM summarises + decomposes prompts, re-routes high-risk queries to zero-trust models.
 - dev.to "PII-aware routing": practitioner pattern -- regex + pseudonyms + routing table, no ML.

apf already produces the PII-sensitivity signal (detector + vault tier counts + locked-category scan), so the auto-route trigger is nearly free: a threshold on per-request vault tier counts or a locked-category hit. Missing piece is the upstream-switch mechanism + per-use-case config.

OPEN for brainstorm with user: (1) build ON LiteLLM (apf in front / as plugin) vs extend apf endpoint_policy.py; (2) manual-switch UX (per agent-skill / MCP / in-prompt); (3) auto-route policy: recommend vs hard-route, and the threshold. Not started beyond this survey.

title: Crowd-improvable filter tuning — users test + improve detection in operation
description: Idea (user, 2026-05-20, for later): a system where users can test and improve the filter while running it in operation, and detection/tuning improvements + filter extensions flow back into the whole system easily and verifiably. Community-sourced detector improvements behind a verification gate, so the overall system improves from real-world use. Needs proper research (prior art: crowdsourced spam/abuse filters, rule-sharing systems, how detection rulesets are community-maintained elsewhere) and brainstorming before any design.
notes:
PRIOR-ART SURVEY 2026-05-21. Crowd-improvable detection has strong, directly transferable prior art -- the model to copy is security-detection rule-sharing, not ad-block lists.

 - CrowdSec: closest match. New rules run in SHADOW MODE (evaluated, not yet acting), human-in-the-loop review, expert system can simulate/replay rulesets -- explicitly to catch data-poisoning. Shadow-mode + replay IS the verification gate apf-hiq wants.
 - Sigma (SigmaHQ): 3000+ community detection rules, peer-reviewed by detection engineers, portable rule format. Model for an apf-rule format + PR-based peer review.
 - VirusTotal Crowdsourced YARA Hub / Elastic detection-rules: public repos, contributors submit + filter + track rules. Model for distribution/discovery.
 - Known pitfall (research): crowdsourced filter lists drift to a few contributors using undocumented heuristics -- so verification gate AND per-rule provenance/rationale must be first-class.

Shape this implies for apf: (1) a portable declarative detector-rule format (regex / label / tier / DE+EN test cases bundled) -- apf regex catalog is already close; (2) every contributed rule ships with fixtures and must pass the benchmark with no FP regression before merge (gate = existing benchmarks.run harness); (3) shadow mode -- a contributed rule runs detect-but-do-not-mask locally first, user sees what it WOULD catch; (4) PR-based flow back to the repo.

HARD CONSTRAINT: a "flows back into the whole system" loop must never send user text or detections off-machine -- violates project hard-rule 3 (PII detection stays local). Crowd improvement shares RULES, never DATA. This anchors the design.

OPEN for brainstorm with user: rule format, shadow-mode UX, GitHub-PR-only vs in-app contribution path, trust/verification model. Not started beyond this survey.
