title: APPOINTMENT + IMPLICIT_PII score tp=0 on ai4privacy — taxonomy mismatch or dead labels?
description:
From the 2026-05-20 FP benchmark: both APPOINTMENT (fp=28 tp=0) and IMPLICIT_PII (fp=7 tp=0) score zero true positives against ai4privacy gold on the 250-mix. Almost certainly because ai4privacy's taxonomy has no equivalent gold label, so every detection scores FP by definition.

Confirm that's the cause (inspect a few flagged spans against the fixtures). If it is pure taxonomy mismatch, the benchmark scoring should arguably exclude these labels when scoring against ai4privacy-derived fixtures, so the precision number isn't artificially depressed. If instead the labels genuinely never fire correctly anywhere (check against the private + content fixtures, which DO use apf taxonomy), reconsider whether emitting them is worth the FP cost.

Acceptance: a decision recorded — either (a) scoring adjustment for taxonomy-mismatched labels, or (b) the labels are validated against apf-taxonomy fixtures and kept/dropped on that evidence.
close_reason: INVESTIGATION RESULT — decision: KEEP both labels. APPOINTMENT and IMPLICIT_PII are legitimate apf-taxonomy labels: content.jsonl gold has 4 APPOINTMENT + 8 IMPLICIT_PII instances. The tp=0 on the 250-mix benchmark is a pure scoring artifact — ai4privacy_sample.jsonl (200 of the 250 records) has ZERO APPOINTMENT/IMPLICIT_PII gold, so the detector's detections on ai4privacy text all score FP by definition. Not dead labels, not real over-detection. Already documented as taxonomy-mismatch in docs/sessions/2026-05-20-fp-benchmark.md. Optional future refinement (not required): a benchmark-scoring mode that excludes apf-only labels when scoring against ai4privacy-derived fixtures, so precision numbers aren't artificially depressed by taxonomy mixing — file separately if cleaner benchmark numbers are wanted.

title: Terminology: rename 'tokenize/tokenisation' → 'mask/masking' (collides with transformer vocab)
description:
Raised by user 2026-05-19: 'tokenisation' is a confusing term for what apf does because in the LLM/transformer context the word already means 'split text into subword tokens for the model'. apf uses it to mean 'replace PII with a reversible placeholder' — a different operation. The collision makes the codebase + docs harder to talk about.

DECISION (made per user 'hältst dich an empfehlungen' + recommendation): use 'masking'. Rationale: standard term in the data-privacy / data-masking field, short, verb-friendly, no transformer-vocab collision. Reverse operation = 'unmask' / 'restore'. Rejected alternatives: 'pseudonymise' (GDPR-precise but clunky as a verb everywhere), 'referencing' (workable given <REF_N> but less established).

SCOPE — rename the VERB / PROCESS, keep the placeholder-noun:
- tokenize_text → mask_text; detokenize_text → unmask_text
- _tokenise_request_body → _mask_request_body; tokenise_request → mask_request; _tokenise_text → _mask_text; _tokenise_message/_part/_block similar
- apf/tokenizer.py → apf/masker.py; apf/detokenizer.py → apf/unmasker.py (+ update imports)
- TOKEN_RE stays fine as a name OR → REF_RE; _PARTIAL_TOKEN_RE similar
- KEEP: 'vault', the <REF_N> placeholder strings, vault.token / _by_token (the placeholder IS token-like; only the verb collides)
- Docs: THREAT-MODEL-PRIVATE.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, INTEGRATION.md, README.md — update prose
- bd issue history / closed-issue text: leave as-is (historical record)

Big mechanical change — do as one dedicated commit so it is cleanly reviewable / revertable. Tests must stay green throughout.

Acceptance: 'tokenis' no longer appears as a verb for the masking operation in apf/ source or current-state docs; all tests green; one self-contained commit.

title: Detector over-filter triage: 3 false-positives surfaced from apf-zzk negative-prompt expansion
description:
From scripts/smoke_loopback.py negative-case expansion run 2026-05-19 (apf-zzk). Three benign prompts triggered detector false-positives, leading to vault entries that should not exist:

title: Should role=system messages be tokenised? (design question)
description:
Surfaced 2026-05-18 while testing apf-6l8 safety-refusal workarounds.

Current behaviour: apf/openai_shape.py::_tokenise_message walks ALL messages including role=system through the detector. For Anthropic Messages API the equivalent lives in apf/proxy.py and processes the 'system' field the same way.

Pro tokenisation (keep current): A user-supplied agent might have a system prompt that legitimately contains PII (their name, contact, role, employer). Filtering protects this.

Contra tokenisation: For control-plane system prompts — filter explainers, agent personalities, tool-use schemas — tokenisation adds noise (a steady baseline of false-positive entries in EVERY vault) and can confuse models that expect their system-prompt verbatim.

Concrete impact observed in apf-6l8 workaround testing: a benign system prompt explaining the privacy filter produces PERSON=1 + IMPLICIT_PII=3 in every vault, including the negative-no-PII case ('What is 2+2?'). This breaks the assertion 'empty user prompt → empty vault'.

Design options:
1. Status quo: always tokenise.
2. Skip role=system entirely.
3. Configurable per-role policy (filter.toml: 'tokenise_roles = [user, assistant, tool]').
4. Tokenise but record a separate 'system_baseline' in the vault summary so downstream consumers can subtract it (lets the per-message profile metric still work).
5. Tokenise only system messages that look user-supplied (heuristic — e.g. first system message of a new session vs. messages added by a configured proxy).

Option 3 is probably the right product answer; option 2 is the right default for now.

Not blocking apf-6l8 directly — variant B of the explainer prompt works around it. But surfaced as a design question that affects vault-summary semantics and over-filter eval (apf-00s) interpretation.
notes:
RESOLVED 2026-05-19: Option 2 implemented as default behaviour with Option 3 escape-hatch.

- Env var APF_TOKENISE_SYSTEM (default 0 = skip) controls role=system tokenisation
- Anthropic shape: proxy._tokenise_request_body gates the system field
- OpenAI shape: openai_shape.tokenise_request takes tokenise_system kwarg (default False); proxy passes the env value
- Locked-category scan (apf-enr) is INDEPENDENT of the flag — still runs on system messages so never-forward categories are caught regardless
- 6 new pytest cases in apf/system_tokenise_test.py cover both shapes, both directions of the flag, plus array-content system messages
- Existing 14 pytest tests + proxy_test e2e remain green
- docs/INTEGRATION.md §'Pro-Max-Konkrete Anweisung' updated with the new env var

Effect on apf-6l8 workaround: variant B explainer system prompt no longer pollutes the vault with PERSON=1 + IMPLICIT_PII=3 baseline. Negative-PII case 'What is 2+2?' now correctly yields empty vault.

title: Audit log v2: disk persistence + Keychain encryption + retention policy
description:
From THREAT-MODEL-PRIVATE.md §5.7 follow-up; explicitly deferred in apf-ive (v1) close-reason:
'v1 in-memory scaffold: off-by-default, APF_AUDIT_LOG=1 to enable, /v1/sessions/{id}/audit endpoint, counts-only invariant tested. Disk persistence + Keychain encryption deferred to v2 design issue.'

v1 (apf-ive) is in-memory only — log dies with the process. v2 makes it survive restarts and persist long enough for self-review.

Design questions (carried over from apf-ive):
1. Storage location: ~/.local/share/apf/audit.* on Linux/macOS, %APPDATA%\apf\audit.* on Windows. SQLite vs JSONL vs binary?
2. Encryption: macOS Keychain for the key (user-resident, biometric-gateable), Linux Secret Service / GNOME Keyring, Windows DPAPI. Key wraps a file-level encryption (AES-GCM or libsodium secretbox).
3. Retention: configurable rolling window (default: 30 days? 7 days?). Per-session granularity for deletion.
4. Granularity (carry from apf-ive): per-span (text, category, tier, timestamp), per-message (counts only), per-session (summary). v1 is counts-only — v2 needs to decide if full spans are recorded and the consequent attack-surface increase.
5. Access UX: CLI command 'apf log [--since] [--category]'; output redacted by default (categories + counts), --reveal flag for full-span output requires Touch ID / passphrase re-auth.
6. Disable + erase: 'apf log --disable' stops recording; 'apf log --wipe' zeroes the file. Both must be testable.
7. Threat model carry: the file IS a target. Mitigations: encryption at rest, optional auto-rotate on lid-close / lock-screen, optional 'panic flush' bound to a hotkey or system event.

Depends on apf-ive (closed, v1 scaffold). Implement after PoC validation if audit-log proves useful; otherwise this might collapse to 'never persist'.
notes:
RESOLVED 2026-05-19: v2 designed in docs/DESIGN-AUDIT-LOG-V2.md; build deferred pending PoC validation that disk persistence is actually used.

Locked-in design decisions (so the eventual build doesn't re-litigate):

- KEEP counts-only — per-span recording REJECTED (doubles attack surface for marginal self-review value)
- SQLite at OS-standard app-data path (macOS: ~/Library/Application Support/apf/audit.db), not JSONL — needed for indexed --since/--category/--session reads
- File-level AES-256-GCM via Python cryptography lib (NOT SQLCipher — extra native dep for no extra win over encrypting the file blob)
- 32-byte key in macOS Keychain via 'security' CLI / Linux Secret Service / Windows DPAPI via 'keyring' lib
- Default retention 7 days (APF_AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS), lazy sampled prune on ~1% of writes, hard cap MAX_ENTRIES=100k
- CLI: 'apf log [--since|--category|--session|--wipe|--disable|--enable|--stats|--json]'. NO --reveal flag (no values to reveal — removing the flag removes the question)
- REJECTED: panic-flush / lid-close hooks (system-event complexity for marginal protection beyond counts-only + AES-GCM at rest)

Build cost estimate: ~500-800 LOC + cryptography + keyring deps. Defer until any of: user explicitly asks for persistent history, PoC validation needs cross-restart audit, real incident requires after-the-fact audit, or apf-sgz v2 (locked-cat routing) needs separate cloud-vs-local accounting.

title: Extend fixture format to support multi-turn conversations
description:
Current fixture schema (fixtures/*.jsonl) is one record = one text. Cannot represent the 14th proposed scenario from THREAT-MODEL-PRIVATE.md §4 (de-profile-aggregation-01): a chat across 5 turns where each turn introduces one more sensitive value (postcode, employer, child's school, weekly therapy time, partner name), accumulating into a profile.

This is the only fixture form that can test §3.3 (cumulative profile assembly across turns) and the §5.4 diversity-weighted multi-stage warning we decided on.

Schema sketch:
- Single-turn: existing shape, unchanged
- Multi-turn: new top-level field 'turns: [...]', each with 'text' + 'spans' + optional 'role' (user/assistant)
- Loader treats them differently: detector runs per-turn, vault accumulates across turns, evaluation checks both per-turn spans AND a cumulative-profile assertion

Acceptance:
- Loader supports both shapes via discriminator (presence of 'turns' field)
- One example fixture (de-profile-aggregation-01) included in fixtures/private/private.jsonl using new shape
- Cumulative warning threshold logic (apf-80c-adjacent) has a fixture to test against

title: Audit log: local record of categories detected/forwarded per session
description:
From THREAT-MODEL-PRIVATE.md §5.7 — open question.

Should the filter persist a local audit log of what was detected and forwarded?

Pro: User can self-review their leak history ('what does Claude know about me'), debug over-filtering, verify the filter is working as expected, learn their own data flow.

Contra: Concentrated log file is itself a target. If an attacker gains local access (stolen laptop, malware, family member), the audit log is a one-stop summary of everything sensitive the user has ever processed.

Design questions:
1. Storage: encrypted at rest? Keyed how? OS keychain, login password, separate passphrase?
2. Retention: days, weeks, indefinite? User-configurable rolling window?
3. Granularity: per-span (text, category, tier, timestamp), per-message (counts only), per-session (summary)?
4. Surface: file in ~/.local/share/apf/? CLI command 'apf log'? UI?
5. Disable mechanic: env var, config? Off-by-default or on-by-default?

Trade-off framing for the doc: more granular = more debug value AND more attack surface. Recommendation default if not decided: on, per-message counts only, no plaintext spans, 30-day rolling window, encrypted via keychain.

NOT a v1 blocker. Decided after first user testing reveals which mode actually gets used.
